threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local Rust DOCX processing engine with a native CLI, PyO3 Python library/CLI, wasm-bindgen browser/Node bindings, a Node CLI, and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Normal document processing transforms caller-supplied package/Markdown bytes into document views, edits, tracked changes, PDF/PNG, and reports. Native CLI startup dispatches shared commands on an 8 MiB worker stack; Python wraps the Rust engine, and Node explicitly performs filesystem I/O around WASM calls. The MCP adapter additionally brokers root-confined document reads and output publication. Explicit self-update and maintainer publication are separate privileged workflows. Evidence: Cargo.toml:83-99; src/bin/jubarte.rs:3555-3583; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:5-15; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:77-97; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-73,106-111; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381. Scope is current source under repository '.', userContext=null; no supplied threat model or knowledge base.
assets: Confidential document text, revisions, comments, metadata, images, embedded fonts, generated DOCX/PDF/PNG, patches, and reports. These cross API and MCP responses and caller-selected filesystem outputs. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,161-218,220-255.

Host process availability and memory/CPU; default admission permits 64 MiB compressed/per-part and 256 MiB inflated, while comparison and native PDF layout use the roomier 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB inflated policy. Both cap entries at 10,000 and XML nesting at 256. XML tag limits are 1,024 attributes, 1,024 name bytes, 64 MiB value bytes, and 128 MiB start-tag bytes. Evidence: src/admission.rs:63-100; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:49-57; src/document_comparer.rs:4926-4927; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778.

Filesystem authority granted to the MCP root, ambient CLI paths, Markdown resource directory, native font directories, and persistent font index. MCP document/output authority is a held cap_std directory; native font discovery/cache accesses remain ambient. Evidence: src/publication.rs:146-165,175-199,203-218; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2858-2871,2936-2943; src/convert/font.rs:2258-2276,2633-2652,3095-3107,3182-3227.

Installed native jubarte executable and release/package integrity. Self-update currently trusts GitHub release assets plus SHA256SUMS.txt without a compiled signing key; the extracted candidate must be a regular file. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257,307-320.

Maintainer publication credentials and GitHub/Jules capabilities: GitHub release contents-write token, optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, local Cargo/npm/PyPI credentials, JULES_API_KEY, and review/comment/check permissions. References only; no credential contents inspected. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:230-263,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-389,919-937,1069; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:46-54,259-324.

Shared self-hosted build infrastructure and remote compilation cache configured at http://mbx-cache:7543, namespace jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines; build integrity and runner isolation depend partly on components absent from this repository. Evidence: .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86; .github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-22,33-52.
trustBoundaries: Document supplier to Rust parsers: DOCX/legacy DOC/XML/images/fonts are untrusted data. Admission checks archive metadata and names, duplicate identities, supported compression/encryption, structural ZIP defects, bounded inflation and XML policy before ordinary downstream processing. No document parts are extracted to disk by admission. The checked XML APIs validate before constructing DOM nodes; public infallible parse_xdocument deliberately does not enforce policy. Evidence: SECURITY.md:38-74; src/admission.rs:13-28,439-548; src/opc/archive.rs:35-51; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-135.

Admission policy to actual consumers: comparison supports caller overrides over InputLimits::compare; WASM retains the same 2 GiB default despite documenting that it exceeds a 32-bit heap. PDF layout also calls admit_package and therefore uses comparison limits. Archive limits govern admitted processing, while native/Python/Node CLI input files are initially read into memory using ambient filesystem APIs. Host process and ingress quotas remain separate responsibilities. Evidence: jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:63-97; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:65-79; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2742; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-81; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-68.

MCP client to document filesystem: startup expands/resolves --root, defaulting to cwd, and opens one native _OutputRoot. Each document path passes an early containment diagnostic and is then read relative to the held capability. Output publication validates portable relative paths, uses capability-relative parent traversal, refuses output symlinks, and honors overwrite. This is distinct from advisory MCP ToolAnnotations, and from the ambient filesystem authority available to native/Python/Node CLIs. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-218,431-463.

MCP edit/render request to publication: docx_edit computes clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json and optional redline.pdf/redline-page-NN.png under root/out_dir; docx_render computes page-NN.png and optional render.pdf. All files stage and validate before commits, but replacement is atomic per file, not across the set; commit errors can report already committed files. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:161-218,229-255; src/publication.rs:168-174.

Markdown image target to native CLI resource authority: --resource-path overrides the Markdown source's parent directory, with '.' for a bare input filename. The loader decodes targets, refuses URL schemes, canonicalizes containment, and reads through an OutputRoot capability. Library DocxOptions defaults to no image loader, making any supplied callback a separate host-granted capability. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2871,2936-2943; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-177,196-198,216-226.

Document font names to native host font resources: rendering resolves fonts through installed/system/Word/cloud and configured per-user directories. The cloud family component must be exactly one normal path component, but native font I/O and the persistent index are not governed by the MCP document OutputRoot. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides the platform directory; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the cache, with empty/off disabling it. Otherwise the cache is font-index.tsv in the parent of the effective font directory. Defaults resolve to ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or ~/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Linux, and %APPDATA%/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Windows. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2258-2276,2281-2315,2633-2652,2855-2862,3095-3107,3154-3168,3182-3227.

Package relationships to resource consumers: document processing uses package part lookups rather than granting general network/file fetches from relationship targets. Representative rendering story/auxiliary-part selection filters External relationships, while altChunk loading resolves targets into package bytes. This is different from native host font reads and explicitly authorized self-update networking. Evidence: SECURITY.md:70-74; src/convert/mod.rs:789-793,21283-21319.

Operator to installed executable: only explicit self-update dispatch invokes updater installation. The updater fixes owner/repository to jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, selects five desktop OS/architecture targets and archive child jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe], verifies SHA256SUMS.txt, applies configured signature policy, and checks the extracted candidate with symlink_metadata before swap. --check does not install; a terminal confirmation or --yes authorizes replacement, and explicit --version permits downgrade. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None currently disable signature enforcement. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:3892-3896; src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,144-160,198-257,307-320.

Release maintainer to public distribution: v* tags trigger read-only binary/wheel build jobs and a contents-write publication job. Optional signing receives ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY only in the signer step, decodes keys into $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN, signs dist/jubarte-*.tar.gz and dist/jubarte-*.zip before checksums, and verifies against committed keys/*.pub. Publication attaches dist/* to the current repository/tag. Local scripts/release.sh additionally uses Cargo/npm/PyPI credentials, mandatory security-check.sh, an explicit version confirmation unless --yes, and a separately configured external app checkout. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-89,230-310,317-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-389,655-660,777-784,875-919,934-937,1069.

PR source to self-hosted CI and remote cache: the docs workflow runs pull_request source on self-hosted runners and invokes a local composite action configuring a pinned external mbx action at http://mbx-cache:7543. The composite's protected-branch-only write claim and private-network-only access are not independently enforced by local source visible here; external action/server and runner provisioning own those controls. The action inserts ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/mbx/bin into PATH and configures a 20 GiB store GC target, separate from server authorization and job isolation. Evidence: .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86,98-99; .github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-22,33-52.

PR review authority is separate from companion remediation authority. The standard Jules reviewer runs for same-repository non-Dependabot PRs, receives JULES_API_KEY and a GitHub token with pull-request/check write permissions, delegates to a pinned external action, and disables approval. The companion workflow resolves a same-repository PR, checks out its exact head SHA, posts a report, and grants creation of a Jules fix session only to trusted author/dispatcher arthrod under specified events. The external session uses AUTO_CREATE_PR, require_plan_approval=false, and a branch name; remote source integration and head/target revision binding are absent implementation details, not established controls. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:46-54,64-102,231-254,259-324.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can choose package entries, XML, relationship strings, embedded media/fonts, Markdown and edit-plan data accepted by the caller, without already owning process credentials, environment variables, filesystem roots, or release infrastructure. Parser failure could add process denial of service or unintended host resource access; ordinary requested document transformations are not privilege escalation. Evidence: SECURITY.md:38-74; src/admission.rs:439-548.

An MCP client can invoke registered tools and choose paths, output directories, edit plans, and overwrite flags within the host-granted root. This adapter supplies no per-tool tenant/identity partition; its transport is stdio, and selecting the root is host authority. Potential boundary failure concerns resources outside that grant, not access already intentionally granted within it. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-160,373-381.

A Markdown author can name image targets; native CLI containment limits that capability to the caller-selected resource directory. A library-supplied image callback may grant different authority and must be evaluated as host code. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2871,2936-2943; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-163,196-198.

Control of JUBARTE_FONT_DIR, JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX, host font files or the existing font index requires an additional local configuration/state capability; it must not be inferred from control of a document's font names. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3107,3154-3168,3182-3227.

A release-asset publisher can affect archive and colocated checksum integrity under today's checksum-only updater policy. This requires release publication compromise or equivalent trusted distribution control, not an ordinary document. A signing-key holder or privileged release runner has separate authority. Evidence: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48,245-257.

PR authors can provide code and review text. Review/remediation workflows restrict same-repository access, while self-hosted PR CI is a separate boundary whose runner/cache network isolation is not established by workflow permissions. Companion-session spending additionally requires the configured trusted author/dispatcher condition. Evidence: .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-39; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-269.
securityObjectives: Refuse unsupported, structurally inconsistent or over-budget packages before downstream inflation/DOM processing, and use checked XML APIs for new untrusted raw-XML consumers. Preserve the intentionally unchecked API contract rather than treating its existence as a defect. Evidence: src/admission.rs:439-548; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-135,919-954.

Keep MCP document reads and requested outputs inside the host-granted directory through actual capability-relative I/O, rather than relying only on string containment or tool visibility hints. Preserve overwrite policy and report partial commit/durability outcomes honestly. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75-108; src/publication.rs:146-199,431-463.

Keep native CLI Markdown image reads within the caller-selected resource authority and avoid fetching document-supplied URLs. Treat ambient CLI paths, library callbacks and native font access as separate capabilities. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2871,2936-2943; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-163; src/convert/font.rs:2258-2276,3182-3227.

Apply caller-owned ingress, memory and CPU limits for shared services, Python hosts and browser/WASM usage; package admission is not a process sandbox or full denial-of-service guarantee. Evidence: SECURITY.md:71-74; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:80-85.

Bind self-update to the selected repository, version, platform archive and regular-file candidate; require actual compiled trusted keys before claiming publisher-independent signature authentication. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,198-257,307-320.

Keep release signing credentials limited to the signing step, preserve signature-before-checksum ordering, and retain publication permissions only in the publishing job. External release scripts/checkouts and package registries remain trusted privileged consumers. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:230-310,317-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-389.

Keep automated review, PR commenting/check writing, companion branch creation, self-hosted job execution and cache publication as distinct authorities with separately established controls. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324; .github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-22.
assumptions: This is source-backed architecture mapping, not a completed vulnerability audit. No application execution, network requests, attack inputs, modifications, or history review were performed. The applicable SECURITY.md resolved to the root policy for '.', src, jubarte-python, jubarte-wasm and .github.

No observed production service, remote tenant model, runner provisioning, filesystem mounts, deployment environment values, or caller process quotas were supplied. Effective platform paths are configuration expressions, not claims about the reviewing machine's actual values.

Documentation/current-control distinction: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:32-35 describes signatures once signing is enabled; its explicit staged policy at docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69-80 agrees with current RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None at src/update.rs:44-48. Signature support must not be reported as currently required authentication. Whether a release secret exists remotely is unknown and unnecessary to establish the updater's compiled policy.

MCP scope distinction: mcp_server.py:7-9,45-46 promises argument/output paths under root, and native capability I/O supports that claim. Interpreting it as process-wide filesystem confinement would exceed the implementation: native font files and font-index.tsv are consumed via ambient fs APIs. The index default follows the parent of effective JUBARTE_FONT_DIR, so a custom '/some/fonts' directory derives '/some/font-index.tsv'. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3107,3182-3227.

MCP publication is staged before committing but atomic only per file; this does not establish rollback of an entire output set after a commit failure. Evidence: src/publication.rs:168-174. docx_edit's all-or-nothing anchor refusal is a separate pre-publication engine guarantee; mcp_server.py:163-168.

Cache claim versus visible enforcement: .github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-12 claims only private-network runners reach a tokenless HTTP server and only protected-branch pushes publish. The local configuration at lines 17-22 supplies URL/namespace to an external pinned action; server ACLs, external action enforcement and runner network isolation are not present here. No unauthorized cache write is established. Runner network access and checkout reuse are documented rather than live-inspected.

The pinned external Jules actions are implementation gaps for remote tool/session permissions, provider credential handling and exact revision binding. Workflow-side grants and filters are established; broader restrictions are not. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:35-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324.

Local release app execution resolves JUBARTE_APP_DIR, otherwise repository-relative jubarte-app, then executes scripts/release-engine.sh with version and --engine-dir $PWD; that checkout is explicitly untracked by this repository. Its downstream deployment credentials and controls are unknown. Evidence: scripts/release.sh:382-389.

The updater delegates HTTPS/download/extraction/replacement internals to self_update with rustls and platform archive features. Wrapper configuration and its regular-file verification hook were inspected; dependency extraction internals were not independently reviewed in this architecture pass. Evidence: Cargo.toml:141-148; src/update.rs:198-210,307-320.

findings.title: Rendering a relationship-selected XML part can bypass the depth limit and abort the host
findings.summary: A document can place deeply nested numbering XML in a .bin part and reference it with the numbering relationship. Admission skips its XML policy; rendering later passes it to the recursive unchecked DOM parser, allowing a small input to overflow the host stack.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled document bytes reach unbounded recursion through an ordinary conversion API. Process availability impact is medium and likelihood is high once the document is converted; no remote deployment is assumed.

confidence.rationale: Static trace establishes suffix-based admission, arbitrary relationship target selection, and recursive parsing without a depth guard. No crash input was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Admission checks XML by filename suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: An auxiliary .bin part is only drained and charged to the inflation budget; its XML depth and tag policy are never inspected.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship type selects an arbitrary part name
codeEvidence.explanation: A numbering relationship may point to a non-.xml internal part; no suffix or content-policy check is applied here.

codeEvidence.label: Numbering loader invokes unchecked DOM parser
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected part bytes become a string and enter Dom::parse_xdocument regardless of their filename.

codeEvidence.label: Unchecked parser recurses for each nested element
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested '<' adds another parse_element stack frame without checking InputLimits.

rootCause.summary: admit classifies auxiliary XML by filename suffix, while main_rel_part classifies it by relationship type. load_numbering bridges those inconsistent classifications and sends the unvalidated bytes to parse_xdocument, whose parse_element calls itself for every nested element. The main-part fallback check does not protect auxiliary numbering parts.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag policy to every relationship-selected XML consumer before constructing its DOM, or classify all XML content types during admission and retain checked depth at each unchecked consumer.

limitations: No runtime crash reproduction; affected thread stack size and host isolation determine failure threshold.
validation.summary: with_layout admits input at src/convert/mod.rs:776, then opens the same package and reaches collect_blocks at :923. collect_blocks calls load_numbering at :7734. A valid internal numbering relationship to a .bin part passes admission's byte limits and main-part check yet reaches unchecked recursive parsing. strict_to_transitional_docx_within only rewrites .xml/.rels names (:810) and PartFs read_package only applies metadata checks to [Content_Types].xml/.rels (:354). Neither inserts the missing depth check.
counterevidence: Ordinary .xml/.rels parts are depth-checked; the main document is explicitly checked even with a different extension.
ZIP entry/part/total byte limits and process limits reduce blast radius but do not bound recursive depth of this auxiliary part.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> admit suffix filter -> internal numbering relationship -> part_string -> parse_numbering_xml -> recursive parse_element
dataflow.source: Attacker-controlled auxiliary package part and relationship
dataflow.outcome: Stack exhaustion terminates the processing thread/process, including an embedding Python host.

impact.why: Availability loss of the process converting the document.

likelihood.why: The attacker chooses both relationship target and deeply nested part bytes; current parser has no guard.

reachability.summary: An untrusted-document supplier needs the victim to call a normal PDF/PNG/render-report conversion; no filesystem or configuration privileges are required.
preconditions: Victim converts the supplied package; it contains valid root metadata and main document.

attackPath.summary: Supply an otherwise valid DOCX with an internal numbering relationship targeting word/numbering.bin containing deeply nested XML; ask the library or CLI to render it.

remediationTests: Verify that rendering refuses a numbering relationship targeting deeply nested .bin XML with INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Apply the same regression to renamed styles, headers, footers, notes, settings and other relationship-selected XML parts.

findings.title: Permitted pull requests execute code on shared self-hosted infrastructure
findings.summary: Pull-request jobs execute the PR checkout, including a mutable local action and Cargo code, on self-hosted runners used by trusted branch jobs. The committed action describes a shared persistent checkout/store and tokenless private-network cache; permitting an attacker PR run grants runner filesystem and network authority.

severity.rationale: Impact can be high for the runner account and private build infrastructure, but likelihood depends on fork-run approval and runner-group/isolation settings unavailable offline. The source does not establish access to release credentials.

confidence.rationale: PR trigger, self-hosted execution and local checkout execution are explicit. Shared private cache/persistence are documented in the committed action; live isolation and approval policy were not inspected.

codeEvidence.label: Pull requests trigger the shared CI workflow
codeEvidence.explanation: No trusted-ref or fork condition restricts this trigger.

codeEvidence.label: PR checkout runs on self-hosted infrastructure
codeEvidence.code:
lint:
    name: fmt + clippy
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@89b12181fb390509a0842a86cc55eeb8eb928c1d # stable branch, pinned 2026-10-01
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
          # jubarte-wasm is linted for the target it ships on.
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
      - uses: ./.github/actions/mbx
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
codeEvidence.explanation: Checkout selects the PR merge tree; the local action and Cargo build execute attacker-editable code with runner authority.

codeEvidence.label: Cache endpoint is shared and unauthenticated by design
codeEvidence.code:
# The self-hosted runners share one mbx cache server on their private Docker
# network (`mbx-cache`), so a crate one runner compiled is a cache hit on the
# others. The server takes no token: mbx sends none over plain HTTP, and only
# the runners can reach it. mbx publishes only from pushes to a protected
# branch; pull requests read. GitHub-hosted runners cannot reach the server,
# so jobs that also run there keep Swatinem/rust-cache on those legs.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: jdx/mr-boxington-action@47ce49b32025d93a7a2f4570815afaa2b7092240 # v1.7.2
      with:
        backend: remote
        version: "1.24.1"
        remote-url: http://mbx-cache:7543
        namespace: jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines
codeEvidence.explanation: Committed topology describes private-network access from runners and configures the cache consumer's concrete HTTP endpoint.

codeEvidence.label: Runner checkout and store are reused
codeEvidence.code:
# Every job on a runner builds in the same checkout, so mbx always counts
    # that checkout's managed target as the most recently used and never
    # collects it: on 2026-10-17 three of them reached 69-220 GiB in a few
    # hours and filled the disk the four runners share. Each job now starts
    # from an empty target, restored from the store and the cache server,
    # and each runner's store keeps to a fixed share of the disk.
codeEvidence.explanation: The documented shared writable resources bridge PR execution and later jobs.

rootCause.summary: The workflow assigns unreviewed PR source to the same self-hosted execution class used for main and executes a repository-local composite action. Read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and disabled checkout credential persistence do not sandbox those commands. The private-cache reader convention is client-side and cannot restrain arbitrary commands supplied by the PR.

findings.remediation: Move every untrusted PR job to hosted or disposable isolated runners without private trusted-network access or shared writable state. Enforce trusted-ref restrictions for persistent runner groups and expose only a separately isolated server-enforced read-only cache to PR jobs.

limitations: No workflow was run and no host/network endpoint contacted.
validation.summary: Validated the unrestricted pull_request trigger and self-hosted lint/test/coverage jobs in ci.yml and corresponding docs, md-roundtrip and adoption jobs. The local mbx action can itself be changed by a PR. Its consumers use http://mbx-cache:7543 and reusable local state. No per-PR execution isolation is defined in this repository.
counterevidence: Some fork runs may require GitHub approval; exploitation requires a permitted run.
Workflow contents permission is read-only and checkout does not retain credentials.
Runner deployment and cache server implementation are external; credential access or successful cache poisoning was not demonstrated.

dataflow.summary: PR checkout -> local action/Cargo invocation -> self-hosted runner process -> runner files/private network
dataflow.outcome: Execution with infrastructure authority beyond submitting source.

impact.why: Arbitrary commands can access the runner account and private build infrastructure.

likelihood.why: Approval and runner isolation prerequisites are external and unknown.

reachability.summary: Requires a PR run permitted by repository approval and runner access policy. Persistence/network exposure follows the committed topology; stronger external isolation would reduce impact.

attackPath.summary: Author a PR changing a local action or Cargo build script; once its run is permitted, the self-hosted job executes it with runner authority.

remediationTests: Assert fork/untrusted PR workflows cannot select persistent trusted runners.
Verify PR worker disposal and separation from main/release writable state and private cache administration.

originalCandidates.originalReport: Public-repo pull_request CI executes attacker-controlled checkout on self-hosted runner without fork/trust gate. .github/workflows/ci.yml:16,36-49; docs.yml PR trigger+self-hosted+run scripts/gen_docs.sh; md-roundtrip/adoption same. .github/actions/mbx/action.yml says runners share private Docker network, tokenless HTTP mbx-cache:7543, and same checkout/store. Fork PR can change build.rs/local action/tests/scripts to execute runner commands when GitHub permits the run, reach private network/poison persistent host for protected jobs. persist-credentials:false/read-only token do not constrain host execution.

fullResult.title: Untrusted pull requests execute on persistent self-hosted runners
fullResult.attacker: Fork PR author whose run is permitted by GitHub repository-level approval settings
fullResult.impact: Runner-account execution, private Docker network access, possible interference with later jobs. Credential theft/protected-build compromise not established offline.
counterevidence: contents:read and persist-credentials:false restrict workflow token only
No live runner inspection; persistence/network facts from committed action
fullResult.remediation: Isolate untrusted jobs on ephemeral runners without trusted network/shared state; server-enforced read-only cache.

fullResult.title: Untrusted pull requests execute on persistent self-hosted runners
fullResult.attacker: Fork PR author whose run is permitted by GitHub repository-level approval settings
fullResult.impact: Runner-account execution, private Docker network access, possible interference with later jobs. Credential theft/protected-build compromise not established offline.
counterevidence: contents:read and persist-credentials:false restrict workflow token only
No live runner inspection; persistence/network facts from committed action
fullResult.remediation: Isolate untrusted jobs on ephemeral runners without trusted network/shared state; server-enforced read-only cache.

findings.title: Rendering a tiny HTML table can exhaust memory through unbounded colspan expansion
findings.summary: An HTML or MHT altChunk cell may supply any positive usize colspan. The converter turns that value into one generated XML grid column per unit after package admission, permitting billions of allocations/emissions from a short input.

severity.rationale: Availability impact is medium and attacker control is direct/high likelihood when the supplied document is converted. Input byte limits do not constrain the numeric multiplier.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified package-to-altChunk flow, unrestricted numeric parsing, and the emission loop; no runtime trigger executed.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship bytes become generated WML
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-supplied chunk bytes are decoded as HTML and passed into html_to_wml.

codeEvidence.label: Colspan has no practical upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: A large representable positive attribute is retained as a cell span.

codeEvidence.label: Every claimed column generates another element
codeEvidence.explanation: The row span sum determines cols, and the converter appends one gridCol per column without a generated-output budget.

rootCause.summary: Builder::start parses colspan as usize and applies only a lower bound. Builder::end_table sums those values and loops to cols, creating XML after admission. Admission's source byte/depth budgets and raster limits therefore cannot bound this expansion.

findings.remediation: Bound colspan and total columns to a practical supported maximum before emission, sum with checked arithmetic, and enforce a cumulative generated-content budget across all altChunks.

limitations: No allocation or hang reproduction was run.
validation.summary: with_layout (:776-799) admits the DOCX, then loads altChunk relationship bytes and expands them before DOM/layout. expand calls html_to_wml. A table with a single large positive colspan reaches end_table's grid emission with no upper or cumulative output check. Values fitting both 32-bit and 64-bit usize can request billions of columns.
counterevidence: Unparseable, negative, and zero spans fall back to one; large positive representable spans do not.
Caller process quotas contain host impact but do not prevent conversion termination.
The original investigator's span location was corrected to :562-566; original report retained.

dataflow.summary: DOCX altChunk -> chunk_html -> html_to_wml -> cell span -> cols -> repeated gridCol writes
dataflow.outcome: Excessive CPU/memory consumption or process termination.

likelihood.why: Short caller-controlled numeric attribute directly drives loop bound.

reachability.summary: Normal library/CLI/Python rendering reaches expansion before selecting pages or emitting outputs.

attackPath.summary: Provide a valid DOCX containing a tiny internally related HTML/MHT table with a huge positive colspan, then request PDF/PNG or render-report conversion.

remediationTests: Refuse an admitted HTML altChunk with a huge positive colspan before generating grid XML.
Cover summed-span overflow and repeated/nested tables under a shared output budget.
